headline: Hanbing Gao
text: Long post alert 📢 This month marks my 1st year of living in Germany 🇩🇪 September 2025, I moved from Tokyo to Berlin after almost 7 years in Japan. Looking back, some of my achievements are perhaps a little unconventional: - I’ve finally made peace with delayed trains and missing trams. 🚋 - Since joining Evamo, my German has improved dramatically. I can now hold conversations confidently, even when I know I’m making mistakes. Turns out, confidence helps. 😉 - I’ve had a few full German conversations with handymen. Somehow, that felt like a real milestone. - I’ve finally learned to be patient (still learning...) and managed to get a Termin with LEA Berlin without submitting multiple Notfall Kontakt forms. This one deserves its own trophy. 🏆 - I’ve made some local friends and built a more meaningful network. - I’ve learned to appreciate nature more. 🌱 - Last but not least, I’ve learned to value family time more. I’ve already booked my second trip back to China within just one year. Shamelessly admitting that I didn’t do this nearly as often when I was in Japan, even though it was much closer. But beyond these little achievements, the past year has made me reflect on something bigger - be comfortable with uncomfortable things Moving to Germany meant almost everything is new - routines, culture, language, connections and more. All of these are something I definitely have underestimated it on my day 1…. But I just have to accept that sometimes I just simply wouldn’t know how things work, which has been one of the most valuable(yet challenging) parts of the experience. I’ve become more comfortable with not being perfect (although my ENTJ side still demands it to be….), asking questions, making mistakes and figuring things out along the way. Also, just a few months ago, I probably would have waited until my German was “good enough” before speaking. Today, I just speak. 😅 Maybe that’s the biggest change of all: I’ve stopped waiting until I feel ready. One year down. Many more things to learn, experience and probably complain about…. 😂 What’s something you’ve learned from living abroad that you didn’t expect? #OneYearInGermany #LifeAbroad #PersonalGrowth #LearningByDoing #InternationalCareer … more
